text:
elena-cs: FYI support ticket from ACME — after an Okta SCIM deprovision some users still show up in the app with roles. customer says they see duplicate accounts with different email aliases.

jamal-eng: can you paste the SCIM logs? sounds like either duplicate create or an update that ended up creating a shadow user.

elena-cs: pasted below (redacted). Okta sent two PATCHs within ~3s for the same user: first removed primaryEmail, second added secondaryEmail as primary. Our SCIM endpoint returned 200 for both.

elena-cs: ```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/12345 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

[ { "op": "remove", "path": "emails[type eq \"work\"].value" }, { "op": "add", "value": { "emails": [ { "value": "jo.smith+alt@acme.com", "type": "work" } ] } } ]
```

alex-ops: our user model uses email as unique key by default. If Okta changed email quickly and the second request came in as a create rather than update, we might have created a second user row tied to okta_id=12345 (but different external_id). any chance patch used "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"]?

jamal-eng: logs show our handler did an upsert by email, then a fallback create when upsert failed because email lookup returned nothing for the interim state. race condition.

maya-platform: reproduce plan:
1) Create user in Okta with primary jo.smith@acme.com, push via SCIM.
2) In quick succession, change primary to jo.smith+alt@acme.com and push a remove then add.
3) Observe our SCIM endpoint behavior; check whether we handle "Operations order" semantics.

elena-cs: customer gave timestamps: 2025-11-12T18:02:15Z (remove) and 18:02:17Z (add). they saw two accounts: jo.smith@acme.com (deactivated) and jo.smith+alt@acme.com (active, has role "workspace.admin").

jamal-eng: minimal repro locally confirmed. root cause: our SCIM handler does the following in this order: email lookup -> if not found then create -> otherwise patch. When remove then add race happens, first op clears email, second sees no existing user and creates new one but still ties Okta okta_id to original user metadata leaving permissions inconsistent.

alex-ops: immediate mitigation for customer: manually merge the two accounts in the admin console and remove the role from the duplicate. also run `POST /admin/scim/refresh?user_id=<okta:12345>` to force reconciliation.

jamal-eng: longer-term fix options:
- make upsert by externalId (Okta user.id) authoritative rather than email fallback
- implement SCIM PATCH transactionality or pre-apply full user object read-before-write with optimistic locking
- canonicalize emails (strip plus-tags) when keying users to reduce alias sprawl

maya-platform: prefer externalId approach. Okta provides "id" on the User resource; if present we should match on that before any email-based create. Add a config flag for "scim.useRemoteIdAsPrimary" so existing customers don't change behavior unexpectedly.

elena-cs: customer asks whether 2FA/MFA linkage could make this worse — they use MFA tied to primary email. if email changes, Okta still links MFA to the identity but product shows two accounts.

jamal-eng: MFA metadata is stored on the user record id, so splitting into two rows will orphan auth factors on the original. not ideal. will add a quick check that if incoming SCIM event contains `externalId` or `meta.externalId` we prefer that.

sre-bot: Incident risk: medium. Race create on SCIM can lead to orphaned MFA creds and privilege escalation if the duplicate retains roles. Recommend hotfix rollout to staging then prod during low-traffic window.

alex-ops: hotfix plan: patch SCIM service to: 1) always match on remote Okta id first, 2) if remote id absent fallback to email (canonicalized), 3) add a short mutex on a per-Okta-user-id basis to serialize concurrent patch ops.

jamal-eng: I'll draft PR with tests that simulate concurrent PATCH ops. also add an audit event when we create a second account for the same remote id so CS gets alerts.

elena-cs: customer-facing reply drafted: "We found a race in our SCIM handler that can create a duplicate account when Okta sends near-simultaneous email-change operations. We've provided a manual remediation path (merge + scim refresh) and are rolling a fix to prefer Okta's user.id for reconciliation. ETA for prod rollout: 48h after QA. Will follow up with logs and a runbook." :white_check_mark:

jamal-eng: note for postmortem: include replication of plus-tag alias case and MFA orphan test.

elena-cs: thanks all — I'll send the customer the remediation steps and the ETA.

okta-bot: Notified Okta support thread 8675309 of potential duplicate provisioning pattern.

alex-ops: after rollout we should run a one-time scan: find users with same okta_remote_id across multiple rows and auto-merge or surface in admin UI.

elena-cs: logging the follow-up task in the ticket. closing thread here, will update once prod fix shipped. :handshake:
